title: EKS on Fargate, and Karpenter for provisioning nodes

videos.script: Lesson 11 gave the cluster node groups: a type chosen in advance, and a count. This lesson takes the planning away, in two different ways. {{fargate}} The first is Fargate. Each pod gets a small machine of its own, sized to what the pod asks for, and gone when the pod goes. There is no node to patch. A Fargate profile decides which pods go there, by namespace and by label. {{limits}} The price is in what does not fit. No DaemonSets, nothing privileged, no EBS volumes. And you pay for every pod's requests, rounded up. {{karpenter}} The second is Karpenter. It watches for pods that cannot be scheduled, works out what machine would hold them, and asks EC2 for it directly. Later it packs the pods onto fewer, cheaper machines. {{loops}} Then the two loops side by side: Cluster Autoscaler, which changes a number on a group, and Karpenter, which chooses the machine. For one small batch of pods, the difference is about three hundred and eighty-eight dollars a month. {{moto}} moto stores a Fargate profile but runs no pods, and Karpenter needs a real cluster to run in. So its files are shown, not applied, and the one EC2 call it makes is run against moto.
